checks.name: worker is neither owner, superuser, RLS bypass nor an API actor
managerA cannot execute maintenance or inspect its protected tables
adminA cannot execute maintenance or inspect its protected tables
customerA cannot execute maintenance or inspect its protected tables
managerB cannot execute maintenance or inspect its protected tables
customerB cannot execute maintenance or inspect its protected tables
maintenance credentials cannot start the HTTP identity adapter
worker cannot read raw import payloads or membership tables
trusted erasure queue is idempotent and rejects a cross-tenant customer ID
one worker transaction anonymizes approved requests and marks held requests for review
legal hold removal alone does not silently approve a held deletion request
operator-reviewed requeue applies erasure after the hold is resolved
startup reconciles erased data before the HTTP listener serves customers
repeated reconciliation does not rewrite profiles or invalidate configuration
failed or busy startup maintenance blocks the API listener
mid-run failure rolls back erasure, staging and retries while recording a safe failure
a later retry commits the entire retained pending batch
expired staging clears across tenants and statuses; unexpired previews survive
pruned retry outcomes do not remove durable operation references
twelve-month cleanup removes expired history and dependent events/outbox only
independent workers skip an already-held transaction lock
the same worker cannot overlap two manual runs
a real timer executes cleanup without a manual maintenance call
stopping the schedule drains work and prevents later runs
database restart preserves the erasure queue and ledger, then resumes maintenance
no maintenance or erasure-queue endpoint is exposed to API clients
run evidence contains only counters, timestamps and stable safe errors
a queued erasure for a temporarily missing profile prevents later resurrection

limits: Scheduled only while the fictional local runner is active; no hosted/background OS automation is installed.
Requests enter through a trusted local operator queue, not a real customer authentication flow.
An independent protected deletion-ledger copy and off-device recovery remain operational work.
